system.name: Spindle
system.one_liner: a distributed training system for multi-task multi-modal models that schedules execution via wavefront scheduling

content.subject: how Spindle remaps two MetaOps across GPU islands so the higher-volume data flow becomes intra-island

elements.name: red MetaOp
elements.role: a MetaOp pair with a much larger 20MB flow between them, the one Spindle prioritizes to keep within one island

elements.name: blue MetaOp
elements.role: a MetaOp pair whose two 10MB flows converge on one destination GPU regardless of placement

content.key_idea: Spindle's device placement swaps which MetaOp flow crosses the island boundary, sacrificing a small 1MB flow to keep a much larger 20MB flow intra-island and cut communication cost.

encoding.color_means: yellow/red/blue distinguish the three MetaOps; pale fill = the MetaOp box, darker inner circle = its icon; red arrow = inter-island communication, green arrow = intra-island communication or intra-device copy
encoding.line_style_means: no dashing on arrows; the grey dotted vertical line marks the boundary between the two device islands
encoding.state_means: before vs. after placement are told apart by which arrows are red (crossing the island boundary) vs green (staying within it) in each of the two side-by-side panels
encoding.marker_means: a double (overlapping) circle icon marks a MetaOp whose output fans out along two edges; a single circle marks one with a single edge; the MB number beside each arrow gives that edge's data-flow volume
encoding.emphasis: the same 20MB red-MetaOp edge is drawn red in the left panel and green in the right, visually proving the placement change to the reader
reusable_patterns: two side-by-side topology panels linked by an open chevron arrow to show a before/after remapping
arrow colour recoding (red vs green) to show the same edge crossing or not crossing a partition boundary
numeric data-volume labels beside each edge to justify a placement/scheduling decision
weaknesses: relies on the reader cross-referencing the legend to decode red vs the two shades of green
the yellow MetaOp's newly-crossing edge is not given its own callout even though it is the trade-off the text discusses

evidence: the data flow volume between red MetaOps is significantly higher than that between yellow ones
Spindle prefers to place the data flow between red ones within the island

summary: This figure illustrates how Spindle's device-placement policy assigns MetaOps to GPUs across two device islands. Two side-by-side topology panels, linked by an open arrow, show the same four GPUs and three colour-coded MetaOps (yellow, red, blue) before and after remapping. Each edge between MetaOps carries a data-flow-volume label in MB and is coloured red when it crosses the island boundary (inter-island) or green when it stays within one island (intra-island communication or intra-device copy). In the left, 'before' panel, the high-volume 20MB flow between the two red MetaOps crosses islands while the smaller 1MB yellow flow stays local. In the right, 'after' panel, Spindle swaps the placement so the 20MB red flow becomes intra-island, at the cost of pushing one 1MB yellow flow across the boundary instead, lowering overall communication cost.
summary_zh: 该图示Spindle的设备放置策略：两面板对比重映射前后，红色MetaOp间20MB高流量数据流由跨孤岛(红箭头)变为孤岛内(绿箭头)，代价是让黄色1MB的一条流转为跨孤岛，从而降低总通信开销。
notes: Index measured panels=1 for a figure that plainly draws two side-by-side before/after panels linked by an arrow; kept layout.panels=1 (from the index) while layout.panel_count and content.panels reflect the actual 2. The yellow MetaOp's second edge crossing the island boundary in the 'after' panel is read from the arrow-colour change visible in the figure; the quoted text only states the red-MetaOp prioritization explicitly.
